mn77:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Sanctuary.
mn77:2.1: Now on that occasion a number of very well-known wanderers were staying in the Wanderers’ Park, the Peacocks’ Sanctuary, that is to say—
mn77:2.2: Annabhāra, Varadhara, and Sakuludāyī the Wanderer, as well as other very well-known wanderers.
mn77:3.1: Then when it was morning, the Blessed One dressed, and taking his bowl and outer robe, he went into Rājagaha for alms.
mn77:3.3: ‘It is still too early to wander for alms in Rājagaha.
mn77:3.4: Suppose I went to Sakuludāyī the Wanderer in the Wanderers’ Park, the Peacocks’ Sanctuary?’
mn77:4.1: Then the Blessed One went to the Wanderers’ Park, the Peacocks’ Sanctuary.
mn77:4.2: Now on that occasion Sakuludāyī the Wanderer was sitting together with a large assembly of wanderers who were shouting and making a great uproar and noise, talking many kinds of pointless talk, such as:
mn77:4.3: talk of kings, talk of robbers, talk of ministers, talk of armies, talk of dangers, talk of battles, talk of food, talk of drink, talk of clothes, talk of beds, talk of garlands, talk of scents, talk of relatives, talk of vehicles, talk of villages, talk of towns, talk of cities, talk of countries, talk of women, talk of heroes, talk of streets, talk of wells, talk of the departed, various idle tales, speculation about the world, speculation about the sea, talk of whether things are or are not, and so on.
mn77:4.4: Sakuludāyī the Wanderer saw the Blessed One coming in the distance.
mn77:4.5: Seeing him, he quieted his own assembly:
mn77:4.9: that venerable one likes quiet and speaks in praise of quiet.
mn77:4.10: Perhaps, finding our assembly quiet, he will think it fit to approach.”
mn77:5.1: Then the Blessed One went up to Sakuludāyī the Wanderer.
mn77:5.2: Sakuludāyī the Wanderer said to the Blessed One:
mn77:5.3: “Let the Blessed One come, venerable sir.
mn77:5.4: Welcome to the Blessed One, venerable sir.
mn77:5.5: It is long, venerable sir, since the Blessed One made an occasion to come here.
mn77:5.6: Let the Blessed One be seated, venerable sir;
mn77:5.8: The Blessed One sat down on the seat made ready.
mn77:5.9: And Sakuludāyī the Wanderer took a certain low seat and sat down at one side.
mn77:5.10: The Blessed One then said to Sakuludāyī the Wanderer, as he sat at one side:
mn77:5.11: “What talk are you gathered here for now, Udāyī? And what was your discussion that was left unfinished?”
mn77:6.1: “Let that be, venerable sir, this talk for which we are now gathered here.
mn77:6.2: It will not be hard for the Blessed One to hear about it later too, venerable sir.
mn77:6.3: A few days ago, venerable sir, when ascetics and brahmins of various sects were gathered together, sitting in the debating hall, this discussion arose:
mn77:6.4: ‘It is a gain indeed for the people of Aṅga and Magadha, it is a great gain indeed for the people of Aṅga and Magadha,
mn77:6.5: that these ascetics and brahmins, heads of orders, heads of groups, teachers of groups, well known and famous ford-makers,[^1] regarded as good by many people, have entered upon the rains residence at Rājagaha.
mn77:6.6: There is this Pūraṇa Kassapa, head of an order, head of a group, teacher of a group, well known and famous, a ford-maker regarded as good by many people;
mn77:6.7: he too has entered upon the rains residence at Rājagaha.
mn77:6.8: There is also this Makkhali Gosāla …
mn77:6.12: and the Nigaṇṭha Nātaputta, head of an order, head of a group, teacher of a group, well known and famous, a ford-maker regarded as good by many people;
mn77:6.13: he too has entered upon the rains residence at Rājagaha.
mn77:6.14: There is also this ascetic Gotama, head of an order, head of a group, teacher of a group, well known and famous, a ford-maker regarded as good by many people;
mn77:6.15: he too has entered upon the rains residence at Rājagaha.
mn77:6.16: Now, of these good ascetics and brahmins, heads of orders, heads of groups, teachers of groups, well known and famous ford-makers, regarded as good by many people, which one is honoured, respected, revered, and venerated by his disciples, and in dependence on whom, honouring and respecting him, do his disciples live?’
mn77:6.18: ‘This Pūraṇa Kassapa is head of an order, head of a group, teacher of a group, well known and famous, a ford-maker regarded as good by many people;
mn77:6.19: yet he is not honoured, respected, revered, or venerated by his disciples, nor do his disciples live in dependence on Pūraṇa Kassapa, honouring and respecting him.
mn77:6.20: Once, Pūraṇa Kassapa was teaching the Dhamma to an assembly of several hundred.
mn77:6.21: Then a certain disciple of Pūraṇa Kassapa made a noise, saying:
mn77:6.22: “Sirs, do not ask Pūraṇa Kassapa about this matter;
mn77:6.24: we know it—ask us about this matter;
mn77:6.25: we will answer it for you, sirs.”
mn77:6.26: Once, Pūraṇa Kassapa, waving his arms about and wailing, could not obtain quiet, saying:
mn77:6.27: “Be quiet, sirs, do not make a noise.
mn77:6.28: They are not asking you, sirs, they are asking us;
mn77:6.30: Many of Pūraṇa Kassapa’s disciples, having proved his assertion wrong, departed, saying:
mn77:6.31: “You do not understand this Dhamma and Discipline; I understand this Dhamma and Discipline. How could you understand this Dhamma and Discipline? You have entered upon a wrong way; I have entered upon a right way. I am consistent; you are inconsistent. What should have been said first you said last; what should have been said last you said first. What you thought over so carefully has been overturned. Your assertion has been refuted. You are defeated. Go and try to salvage your doctrine, or disentangle yourself if you can.”
mn77:6.32: So Pūraṇa Kassapa is not honoured, respected, revered, or venerated by his disciples, nor do his disciples live in dependence on Pūraṇa Kassapa, honouring and respecting him.
mn77:6.33: And Pūraṇa Kassapa was reviled with the reviling of the Dhamma.’
mn77:6.39: the Nigaṇṭha Nātaputta is head of an order, head of a group, teacher of a group, well known and famous, a ford-maker regarded as good by many people;
mn77:6.40: yet he is not honoured, respected, revered, or venerated by his disciples, nor do his disciples live in dependence on the Nigaṇṭha Nātaputta, honouring and respecting him.
mn77:6.41: Once, the Nigaṇṭha Nātaputta was teaching the Dhamma to an assembly of several hundred.
mn77:6.42: Then a certain disciple of the Nigaṇṭha Nātaputta made a noise, saying:
mn77:6.43: “Sirs, do not ask the Nigaṇṭha Nātaputta about this matter;
mn77:6.45: we know it—ask us about this matter;
mn77:6.46: we will answer it for you, sirs.”
mn77:6.47: Once, the Nigaṇṭha Nātaputta, waving his arms about and wailing, could not obtain quiet, saying:
mn77:6.48: “Be quiet, sirs, do not make a noise.
mn77:6.49: They are not asking you, sirs, they are asking us;
mn77:6.51: Many of the Nigaṇṭha Nātaputta’s disciples, having proved his assertion wrong, departed, saying:
mn77:6.52: “You do not understand this Dhamma and Discipline; I understand this Dhamma and Discipline. How could you understand this Dhamma and Discipline? You have entered upon a wrong way; I have entered upon a right way. I am consistent; you are inconsistent. What should have been said first you said last; what should have been said last you said first. What you thought over so carefully has been overturned. Your assertion has been refuted. You are defeated. Go and try to salvage your doctrine, or disentangle yourself if you can.”
mn77:6.53: So the Nigaṇṭha Nātaputta is not honoured, respected, revered, or venerated by his disciples, nor do his disciples live in dependence on the Nigaṇṭha Nātaputta, honouring and respecting him.
mn77:6.54: And the Nigaṇṭha Nātaputta was reviled with the reviling of the Dhamma.’
mn77:6.56: ‘This ascetic Gotama too is head of an order, head of a group, teacher of a group, well known and famous, a ford-maker regarded as good by many people;
mn77:6.57: and he is honoured, respected, revered, and venerated by his disciples, and his disciples live in dependence on the ascetic Gotama, honouring and respecting him.
mn77:6.58: Once, the ascetic Gotama was teaching the Dhamma to an assembly of several hundred.
mn77:6.59: Then a certain disciple of the ascetic Gotama cleared his throat.
mn77:6.60: Thereupon a certain companion in the life divine nudged him with his knee, saying:
mn77:6.61: “May the venerable one be quiet, may the venerable one not make a noise; the Teacher, the Blessed One, is teaching the Dhamma.”
mn77:6.62: At the time when the ascetic Gotama is teaching the Dhamma to an assembly of several hundred, there is on that occasion no sound of coughing or clearing of throats among the ascetic Gotama’s disciples.
mn77:6.63: For at that time the great crowd of people is waiting expectantly, thinking:
mn77:6.64: “Let us hear the Dhamma that the Blessed One is about to speak.”
mn77:6.65: Just as if a man were pressing out pure honey at a crossroads where four highways meet,
mn77:6.66: and a great crowd of people were waiting expectantly for it;
mn77:6.67: so too, at the time when the ascetic Gotama is teaching the Dhamma to an assembly of several hundred, there is on that occasion no sound of coughing or clearing of throats among the ascetic Gotama’s disciples.
mn77:6.68: For at that time the great crowd of people is waiting expectantly, thinking:
mn77:6.69: “Let us hear the Dhamma that the Blessed One is about to speak.”
mn77:6.70: And even those disciples of the ascetic Gotama who quarrel with their companions in the life divine and abandon the training and revert to the lower life, even they speak in praise of the Teacher, in praise of the Dhamma, and in praise of the Sangha; they blame only themselves, not others, saying: “We are unlucky, we have little merit, for though we went forth into homelessness in such a well-proclaimed Dhamma and Discipline, we were unable to live the perfect and pure life divine for the rest of our lives.”
mn77:6.71: Becoming monastery attendants or lay followers, they undertake and observe the five precepts.
mn77:6.72: So the ascetic Gotama is honoured, respected, revered, and venerated by his disciples, and his disciples live in dependence on the ascetic Gotama, honouring and respecting him.’”
mn77:7.1: “But, Udāyī, how many things do you see in me on account of which my disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me?”
mn77:8.1: “I see five things in the Blessed One, venerable sir, on account of which his disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate him, and live in dependence on him, honouring and respecting him.
mn77:8.3: First, venerable sir, the Blessed One eats little, and he speaks in praise of eating little.
mn77:8.4: This, venerable sir, is the first thing I see in the Blessed One on account of which his disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate him, and live in dependence on him, honouring and respecting him.
mn77:8.5: Again, venerable sir, the Blessed One is content with any kind of robe, and he speaks in praise of contentment with any kind of robe.
mn77:8.6: This, venerable sir, is the second thing I see in the Blessed One on account of which his disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate him, and live in dependence on him, honouring and respecting him.
mn77:8.7: Again, venerable sir, the Blessed One is content with any kind of almsfood, and he speaks in praise of contentment with any kind of almsfood.
mn77:8.8: This, venerable sir, is the third thing I see in the Blessed One on account of which his disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate him, and live in dependence on him, honouring and respecting him.
mn77:8.9: Again, venerable sir, the Blessed One is content with any kind of resting place, and he speaks in praise of contentment with any kind of resting place.
mn77:8.10: This, venerable sir, is the fourth thing I see in the Blessed One on account of which his disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate him, and live in dependence on him, honouring and respecting him.
mn77:8.11: Again, venerable sir, the Blessed One is secluded, and he speaks in praise of seclusion.
mn77:8.12: This, venerable sir, is the fifth thing I see in the Blessed One on account of which his disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate him, and live in dependence on him, honouring and respecting him.
mn77:8.13: These, venerable sir, are the five things I see in the Blessed One on account of which his disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate him, and live in dependence on him, honouring and respecting him.”
mn77:9.1: “If, Udāyī, my disciples were to honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me, thinking: ‘The ascetic Gotama eats little, and he speaks in praise of eating little’—
mn77:9.2: there are disciples of mine, Udāyī, who live on a cupful of food, or on half a cupful, or on the amount of a bilva fruit, or on half a bilva fruit,[^2] while I sometimes eat the full contents of this bowl or even more.
mn77:9.3: If, Udāyī, my disciples were to honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me, thinking: ‘The ascetic Gotama eats little, and he speaks in praise of eating little’—then those disciples of mine, Udāyī, who live on a cupful of food, or on half a cupful, or on the amount of a bilva fruit, or on half a bilva fruit, would not honour, respect, revere, or venerate me for that reason, nor live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me for that reason.
mn77:9.4: If, Udāyī, my disciples were to honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me, thinking: ‘The ascetic Gotama is content with any kind of robe, and he speaks in praise of contentment with any kind of robe’—
mn77:9.5: there are disciples of mine, Udāyī, who are refuse-rag wearers, wearers of coarse robes, who collect rags from charnel grounds, rubbish heaps, or shops, make them into patched outer robes, and wear them, while I sometimes wear robes given by householders that are so fine that gourd-hair[^3] would seem coarse by comparison.
mn77:9.6: If, Udāyī, my disciples were to honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me, thinking: ‘The ascetic Gotama is content with any kind of robe, and he speaks in praise of contentment with any kind of robe’—then those disciples of mine, Udāyī, who are refuse-rag wearers, wearers of coarse robes, who collect rags from charnel grounds, rubbish heaps, or shops, make them into patched outer robes, and wear them, would not honour, respect, revere, or venerate me for that reason, nor live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me for that reason.
mn77:9.7: If, Udāyī, my disciples were to honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me, thinking: ‘The ascetic Gotama is content with any kind of almsfood, and he speaks in praise of contentment with any kind of almsfood’—
mn77:9.8: there are disciples of mine, Udāyī, who eat almsfood, walking on an uninterrupted almsround, delighting in the practice of gleaning, who, once they have entered a house, do not consent even when invited to sit down, while I sometimes eat, on invitation, fine rice with the dark grains picked out, together with many sauces and curries.
mn77:9.9: If, Udāyī, my disciples were to honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me, thinking: ‘The ascetic Gotama is content with any kind of almsfood, and he speaks in praise of contentment with any kind of almsfood’—then those disciples of mine, Udāyī, who eat almsfood, walking on an uninterrupted almsround, delighting in the practice of gleaning, who, once they have entered a house, do not consent even when invited to sit down, would not honour, respect, revere, or venerate me for that reason, nor live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me for that reason.
mn77:9.10: If, Udāyī, my disciples were to honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me, thinking: ‘The ascetic Gotama is content with any kind of resting place, and he speaks in praise of contentment with any kind of resting place’—
mn77:9.11: there are disciples of mine, Udāyī, who are tree-root dwellers, open-air dwellers, who for eight months do not go under a roof,[^4] while I sometimes live in gabled mansions, plastered within and without, draught-free, with door-bolts fastened and windows shuttered.
mn77:9.12: If, Udāyī, my disciples were to honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me, thinking: ‘The ascetic Gotama is content with any kind of resting place, and he speaks in praise of contentment with any kind of resting place’—then those disciples of mine, Udāyī, who are tree-root dwellers, open-air dwellers, who for eight months do not go under a roof, would not honour, respect, revere, or venerate me for that reason, nor live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me for that reason.
mn77:9.13: If, Udāyī, my disciples were to honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me, thinking: ‘The ascetic Gotama is secluded, and he speaks in praise of seclusion’—
mn77:9.14: there are disciples of mine, Udāyī, who are forest-dwellers, dwelling in remote resting places in forests and woodland thickets, and who come to the midst of the Sangha only once each half-month for the recitation of the Pātimokkha, while I sometimes live surrounded by bhikkhus, bhikkhunīs, male lay followers, female lay followers, kings, kings’ ministers, other sectarians, and other sectarians’ disciples.
mn77:9.15: If, Udāyī, my disciples were to honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me, thinking: ‘The ascetic Gotama is secluded, and he speaks in praise of seclusion’—then those disciples of mine, Udāyī, who are forest-dwellers, dwelling in remote resting places in forests and woodland thickets, who come to the midst of the Sangha only once each half-month for the recitation of the Pātimokkha, would not honour, respect, revere, or venerate me for that reason, nor live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me for that reason.
mn77:9.16: So, Udāyī, it is not by these five things that my disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me.
mn77:10.1: There are, Udāyī, five other things on account of which my disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me.
mn77:10.3: Here, Udāyī, my disciples esteem me for the higher virtue thus:
mn77:10.4: ‘The ascetic Gotama has virtue; he possesses the highest aggregate of virtue.’
mn77:11.1: And in that, Udāyī, my disciples esteem me for the higher virtue thus:
mn77:11.2: ‘The ascetic Gotama has virtue; he possesses the highest aggregate of virtue’—this, Udāyī, is the first thing on account of which my disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me.
mn77:12.1: Again, Udāyī, my disciples esteem me for my superior knowledge and vision thus:
mn77:12.2: ‘The ascetic Gotama, when he knows, says “I know”;
mn77:12.3: when he sees, he says “I see”;
mn77:12.4: the ascetic Gotama teaches the Dhamma by direct knowledge, not without direct knowledge;
mn77:12.5: the ascetic Gotama teaches the Dhamma with a basis, not without a basis;[^5]
mn77:12.6: the ascetic Gotama teaches the Dhamma with its own marvel, not without marvel.’[^6]
mn77:12.7: And in that, Udāyī, my disciples esteem me for my superior knowledge and vision thus:
mn77:12.8: ‘The ascetic Gotama, when he knows, says “I know”;
mn77:12.9: when he sees, he says “I see”;
mn77:12.10: the ascetic Gotama teaches the Dhamma by direct knowledge, not without direct knowledge;
mn77:12.11: the ascetic Gotama teaches the Dhamma with a basis, not without a basis;
mn77:12.12: the ascetic Gotama teaches the Dhamma with its own marvel, not without marvel’—this, Udāyī, is the second thing on account of which my disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me.
mn77:13.1: Again, Udāyī, my disciples esteem me for the higher wisdom thus:
mn77:13.2: ‘The ascetic Gotama has wisdom; he possesses the highest aggregate of wisdom;
mn77:13.3: it is not possible that he should not foresee a future line of argument, or should not be able to refute thoroughly, in accordance with the Dhamma, an opposing doctrine that has arisen.’
mn77:13.5: would my disciples, knowing and seeing thus, break in with a question from time to time?”
mn77:13.7: “I do not expect instruction from my disciples;
mn77:13.8: rather, it is my disciples who expect instruction from me.
mn77:13.9: And in that, Udāyī, my disciples esteem me for the higher wisdom thus:
mn77:13.10: ‘The ascetic Gotama has wisdom; he possesses the highest aggregate of wisdom;
mn77:13.11: it is not possible that he should not foresee a future line of argument, or should not be able to refute an opposing doctrine that has arisen, in accordance with the Dhamma—
mn77:13.13: This, Udāyī, is the third thing on account of which my disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me.
mn77:14.1: Again, Udāyī, when my disciples, overcome by suffering, overwhelmed by suffering, come to me and ask about the noble truth of suffering, being asked I explain to them the noble truth of suffering, and I satisfy their minds with my explanation of the question;
mn77:14.2: they ask me about the origin of suffering …
mn77:14.4: the way leading to the cessation of suffering, being asked I explain to them the noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of suffering, and I satisfy their minds with my explanation of the question.
mn77:14.5: And in that, Udāyī, when my disciples, overcome by suffering, overwhelmed by suffering, come to me and ask about the noble truth of suffering, being asked I explain to them the noble truth of suffering, and I satisfy their minds with my explanation of the question;
mn77:14.6: they ask me about the origin of suffering …
mn77:14.8: the way leading to the cessation of suffering.
mn77:14.9: Being asked, I explain to them the noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of suffering.
mn77:14.10: I satisfy their minds with my explanation of the question.
mn77:14.11: This, Udāyī, is the fourth thing on account of which my disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me.
mn77:15.1: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples develop the four foundations of mindfulness.
mn77:15.2: Here, Udāyī, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body as a body, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, having put away covetousness and grief for the world;
mn77:15.3: he dwells contemplating feelings as feelings …
mn77:15.4: he dwells contemplating mind as mind …
mn77:15.5: he dwells contemplating mental objects as mental objects, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, having put away covetousness and grief for the world.
mn77:15.6: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.
mn77:16.1: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples develop the four right strivings.
mn77:16.2: Here, Udāyī, a bhikkhu arouses zeal, makes an effort, stirs up energy, exerts his mind, and strives for the non-arising of unarisen evil unwholesome states;
mn77:16.3: he arouses zeal, makes an effort, stirs up energy, exerts his mind, and strives for the abandoning of arisen evil unwholesome states;
mn77:16.4: he arouses zeal, makes an effort, stirs up energy, exerts his mind, and strives for the arising of unarisen wholesome states;
mn77:16.5: he arouses zeal, makes an effort, stirs up energy, exerts his mind, and strives for the continuation, non-disappearance, strengthening, increase, and fulfilment by development of arisen wholesome states.
mn77:16.6: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.
mn77:17.1: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples develop the four bases for spiritual power.
mn77:17.2: Here, Udāyī, a bhikkhu develops the basis for spiritual power that possesses concentration due to desire and the volitional formations of striving,
mn77:17.3: he develops the basis for spiritual power that possesses concentration due to energy and the volitional formations of striving,
mn77:17.4: he develops the basis for spiritual power that possesses concentration due to (purity of) mind and the volitional formations of striving,
mn77:17.5: he develops the basis for spiritual power that possesses concentration due to investigation and the volitional formations of striving.
mn77:17.6: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.
mn77:18.1: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples develop the five faculties.
mn77:18.2: Here, Udāyī, a bhikkhu develops the faculty of faith, which leads to peace, leads to enlightenment;
mn77:18.3: he develops the faculty of energy …
mn77:18.4: he develops the faculty of mindfulness …
mn77:18.5: he develops the faculty of concentration …
mn77:18.6: he develops the faculty of wisdom, which leads to peace, leads to enlightenment.
mn77:18.7: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.
mn77:19.1: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples develop the five powers.
mn77:19.2: Here, Udāyī, a bhikkhu develops the power of faith, which leads to peace, leads to enlightenment;
mn77:19.3: he develops the power of energy …
mn77:19.4: he develops the power of mindfulness …
mn77:19.5: he develops the power of concentration …
mn77:19.6: he develops the power of wisdom, which leads to peace, leads to enlightenment.
mn77:19.7: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.
mn77:20.1: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples develop the seven enlightenment factors.
mn77:20.2: Here, Udāyī, a bhikkhu develops the mindfulness enlightenment factor, which is supported by seclusion, by dispassion, by cessation, and ripens in relinquishment;
mn77:20.3: he develops the investigation-of-states enlightenment factor …
mn77:20.4: he develops the energy enlightenment factor …
mn77:20.5: he develops the joy enlightenment factor …
mn77:20.6: he develops the tranquillity enlightenment factor …
mn77:20.7: he develops the concentration enlightenment factor …
mn77:20.8: he develops the equanimity enlightenment factor, which is supported by seclusion, by dispassion, by cessation, and ripens in relinquishment.
mn77:20.9: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.
mn77:21.1: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples develop the noble eightfold path.
mn77:21.2: Here, Udāyī, a bhikkhu develops right view, develops right intention, develops right speech, develops right action, develops right livelihood, develops right effort, develops right mindfulness, develops right concentration.
mn77:21.3: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.
mn77:22.1: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples develop the eight liberations.
mn77:22.4: Not perceiving form in oneself, one sees forms externally:
mn77:22.6: One is intent only on the beautiful:
mn77:22.8: With the complete surmounting of perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of resistance, with non-attention to perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, one enters upon and abides in the base of infinite space:
mn77:22.10: By completely surmounting the base of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, one enters upon and abides in the base of infinite consciousness:
mn77:22.12: By completely surmounting the base of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing’, one enters upon and abides in the base of nothingness:
mn77:22.14: By completely surmounting the base of nothingness, one enters upon and abides in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception:
mn77:22.16: By completely surmounting the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, one enters upon and abides in the cessation of perception and feeling:
mn77:22.18: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.
mn77:23.1: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples develop the eight bases for transcendence.
mn77:23.2: Perceiving form in oneself, one sees forms externally, limited, fair and ugly:
mn77:23.3: ‘having transcended these, I know, I see’—thus one is percipient.
mn77:23.4: This is the first base for transcendence.
mn77:23.5: Perceiving form in oneself, one sees forms externally, measureless, fair and ugly:
mn77:23.6: ‘having transcended these, I know, I see’—thus one is percipient.
mn77:23.7: This is the second base for transcendence.
mn77:23.8: Not perceiving form in oneself, one sees forms externally, limited, fair and ugly:
mn77:23.9: ‘having transcended these, I know, I see’—thus one is percipient.
mn77:23.10: This is the third base for transcendence.
mn77:23.11: Not perceiving form in oneself, one sees forms externally, measureless, fair and ugly:
mn77:23.12: ‘having transcended these, I know, I see’—thus one is percipient.
mn77:23.13: This is the fourth base for transcendence.
mn77:23.14: Not perceiving form in oneself, one sees forms externally, blue, of blue colour, blue in appearance, blue in lustre.
mn77:23.15: Just as a flax flower is blue, of blue colour, blue in appearance, blue in lustre, or just as that cloth from Vārāṇasī, smoothed on both sides, is blue, of blue colour, blue in appearance, blue in lustre—
mn77:23.16: so too, not perceiving form in oneself, one sees forms externally, blue, of blue colour, blue in appearance, blue in lustre.
mn77:23.17: ‘Having transcended these, I know, I see’—thus one is percipient.
mn77:23.18: This is the fifth base for transcendence.
mn77:23.19: Not perceiving form in oneself, one sees forms externally, yellow, of yellow colour, yellow in appearance, yellow in lustre.
mn77:23.20: Just as a kaṇikāra flower is yellow, of yellow colour, yellow in appearance, yellow in lustre, or just as that cloth from Vārāṇasī, smoothed on both sides, is yellow, of yellow colour, yellow in appearance, yellow in lustre—
mn77:23.21: so too, not perceiving form in oneself, one sees forms externally, yellow, of yellow colour, yellow in appearance, yellow in lustre.
mn77:23.22: ‘Having transcended these, I know, I see’—thus one is percipient.
mn77:23.23: This is the sixth base for transcendence.
mn77:23.24: Not perceiving form in oneself, one sees forms externally, red, of red colour, red in appearance, red in lustre.
mn77:23.25: Just as a bandhujīvaka flower is red, of red colour, red in appearance, red in lustre, or just as that cloth from Vārāṇasī, smoothed on both sides, is red, of red colour, red in appearance, red in lustre—
mn77:23.26: so too, not perceiving form in oneself, one sees forms externally, red, of red colour, red in appearance, red in lustre.
mn77:23.27: ‘Having transcended these, I know, I see’—thus one is percipient.
mn77:23.28: This is the seventh base for transcendence.
mn77:23.29: Not perceiving form in oneself, one sees forms externally, white, of white colour, white in appearance, white in lustre.
mn77:23.30: Just as the morning star[^7] is white, of white colour, white in appearance, white in lustre, or just as that cloth from Vārāṇasī, smoothed on both sides, is white, of white colour, white in appearance, white in lustre—
mn77:23.31: so too, not perceiving form in oneself, one sees forms externally, white, of white colour, white in appearance, white in lustre.
mn77:23.32: ‘Having transcended these, I know, I see’—thus one is percipient.
mn77:23.33: This is the eighth base for transcendence.
mn77:23.34: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.
mn77:24.1: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples develop the ten bases of totality.[^8]
mn77:24.2: One perceives the earth-totality, above, below, across, undivided, immeasurable;
mn77:24.11: one perceives the consciousness-totality, above, below, across, undivided, immeasurable.
mn77:24.12: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.
mn77:25.1: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples develop the four jhānas.
mn77:25.2: Here, Udāyī, quite secluded from sensual desires, secluded from unwholesome states, a bhikkhu enters upon and abides in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by initial application and sustained application, with joy and pleasure born of seclusion.
mn77:25.3: He drenches, steeps, fills, and pervades this very body with the joy and pleasure born of seclusion, so that there is no part of his whole body that is not pervaded by the joy and pleasure born of seclusion.
mn77:25.4: Just as, Udāyī, a skilled bathman or his apprentice heaps bath powder in a metal basin and, sprinkling it again and again with water, kneads it together, so that the ball of bath powder is pervaded by moisture, soaked, saturated within and without, yet does not ooze;
mn77:25.5: so too, Udāyī, a bhikkhu drenches, steeps, fills, and pervades this very body with the joy and pleasure born of seclusion, so that there is no part of his whole body that is not pervaded by the joy and pleasure born of seclusion.
mn77:26.1: Again, Udāyī, with the stilling of initial and sustained application, a bhikkhu … enters upon and abides in the second jhāna …
mn77:26.2: He drenches, steeps, fills, and pervades this very body with the joy and pleasure born of concentration, so that there is no part of his whole body that is not pervaded by the joy and pleasure born of concentration.
mn77:26.3: Just as, Udāyī, there might be a lake whose water wells up from below, with no inflow from the east, west, north, or south, and not even replenished from time to time by showers of rain from the sky;
mn77:26.4: then the cool spring of water welling up in that lake would drench, steep, fill, and pervade that very lake with cool water, so that there would be no part of the whole lake that was not pervaded by the cool water;
mn77:26.5: so too, Udāyī, a bhikkhu drenches, steeps, fills, and pervades this very body with the joy and pleasure born of concentration, so that there is no part of his whole body that is not pervaded by the joy and pleasure born of concentration.
mn77:27.1: Again, Udāyī, with the fading away of joy as well … a bhikkhu … enters upon and abides in the third jhāna …
mn77:27.2: He drenches, steeps, fills, and pervades this very body with the pleasure divested of joy, so that there is no part of his whole body that is not pervaded by the pleasure divested of joy.
mn77:27.3: Just as, Udāyī, in a pond of blue lotuses, or a pond of pink lotuses, or a pond of white lotuses, some lotuses that are born in the water and grow in the water do not rise up out of the water but thrive underwater, and cool water drenches, steeps, fills, and pervades them from their tips to their roots, so that there is no part of the whole of those lotuses that is not pervaded by the cool water;
mn77:27.4: so too, Udāyī, a bhikkhu drenches, steeps, fills, and pervades this very body with the pleasure divested of joy, so that there is no part of his whole body that is not pervaded by the pleasure divested of joy.
mn77:28.1: Again, Udāyī, with the abandoning of pleasure and pain, and with the previous disappearance of joy and grief, a bhikkhu enters upon and abides in the fourth jhāna, which has neither-pain-nor-pleasure and purity of mindfulness due to equanimity.
mn77:28.2: He sits pervading this very body with a pure, bright mind, so that there is no part of his whole body that is not pervaded by the pure, bright mind.
mn77:28.3: Just as, Udāyī, a man might be sitting covered from head to foot with a white cloth, so that there would be no part of his whole body not covered by the white cloth;
mn77:28.4: so too, Udāyī, a bhikkhu sits pervading this very body with a pure, bright mind, so that there is no part of his whole body that is not pervaded by the pure, bright mind.
mn77:28.5: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.
mn77:29.1: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples understand thus:
mn77:29.2: ‘This body of mine has form, is made up of the four great elements, is procreated by mother and father, is built up out of rice and gruel, and is subject to impermanence, to being rubbed and massaged, to breaking apart and dispersal;
mn77:29.3: and this consciousness of mine is supported by it and bound up with it.’
mn77:29.4: Just as, Udāyī, there might be a beautiful beryl gem of pure water, eight-faceted, well cut, clear, transparent, possessed of all good qualities,
mn77:29.5: and a thread—blue, yellow, red, white, or pale yellow—were strung through it;
mn77:29.6: and a man with good eyes, taking it in his hand, might review it thus:
mn77:29.7: ‘This beryl gem is beautiful, of pure water, eight-faceted, well cut, clear, transparent, possessed of all good qualities,
mn77:29.8: and a thread—blue, yellow, red, white, or pale yellow—is strung through it.’
mn77:29.9: So too, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples understand thus:
mn77:29.10: ‘This body of mine has form, is made up of the four great elements, is procreated by mother and father, is built up out of rice and gruel, and is subject to impermanence, to being rubbed and massaged, to breaking apart and dispersal;
mn77:29.11: and this consciousness of mine is supported by it and bound up with it.’
mn77:29.12: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.
mn77:30.1: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples create from this body another body, possessing form, mind-made, complete in all its limbs, not deficient in any faculty.
mn77:30.2: Just as, Udāyī, a man might draw a reed out of its sheath;
mn77:30.4: ‘This is the sheath, this is the reed; the sheath is one thing, the reed another; but the reed has been drawn out from the sheath.’
mn77:30.5: Or just as, Udāyī, a man might draw a sword out of its scabbard;
mn77:30.7: ‘This is the sword, this is the scabbard; the sword is one thing, the scabbard another; but the sword has been drawn out from the scabbard.’
mn77:30.8: Or just as, Udāyī, a man might pull a snake out of its slough;
mn77:30.10: ‘This is the snake, this is the slough; the snake is one thing, the slough another; but the snake has been pulled out from the slough.’
mn77:30.11: So too, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples create from this body another body, possessing form, mind-made, complete in all its limbs, not deficient in any faculty.
mn77:30.12: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.
mn77:31.1: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples wield the various kinds of supernormal power: having been one, they become many; having been many, they become one; they appear and vanish; they go unhindered through a wall, through a rampart, through a mountain, as though through space; they dive in and out of the earth as though it were water; they walk on water without sinking as though on earth; seated cross-legged, they travel through the air like a bird on the wing; with their hands they touch and stroke the moon and sun, so mighty and powerful; they wield bodily mastery even as far as the Brahmā world.
mn77:31.2: Just as, Udāyī, a skilled potter or his apprentice could make and fashion from well-prepared clay whatever kind of vessel he wished;
mn77:31.3: or just as, Udāyī, a skilled ivory-carver or his apprentice could make and fashion from well-prepared ivory whatever kind of ivory-work he wished;
mn77:31.4: or just as, Udāyī, a skilled goldsmith or his apprentice could make and fashion from well-prepared gold whatever kind of gold-work he wished;
mn77:31.5: so too, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples wield the various kinds of supernormal power: having been one, they become many; having been many, they become one; they appear and vanish; they go unhindered through a wall, through a rampart, through a mountain, as though through space; they dive in and out of the earth as though it were water; they walk on water without sinking as though on earth; seated cross-legged, they travel through the air like a bird on the wing; with their hands they touch and stroke the moon and sun, so mighty and powerful; they wield bodily mastery even as far as the Brahmā world.
mn77:31.6: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.
mn77:32.1: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples hear, with the divine ear element, purified and surpassing the human, both kinds of sounds, the divine and the human, those that are far as well as near.
mn77:32.2: Just as, Udāyī, a strong conch-blower could make himself heard without difficulty in the four quarters;
mn77:32.3: so too, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples hear, with the divine ear element, purified and surpassing the human, both kinds of sounds, the divine and the human, those that are far as well as near.
mn77:32.4: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.
mn77:33.1: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples, having encompassed the minds of other beings and other persons with their own minds, understand them—
mn77:33.2: they understand a mind with lust as a mind with lust,
mn77:33.3: and a mind without lust as a mind without lust;
mn77:33.4: they understand a mind with hate as a mind with hate,
mn77:33.5: and a mind without hate as a mind without hate;
mn77:33.6: they understand a mind with delusion as a mind with delusion,
mn77:33.7: and a mind without delusion as a mind without delusion;
mn77:33.8: they understand a contracted mind as contracted,
mn77:33.9: and a distracted mind as distracted;
mn77:33.10: they understand an exalted mind as exalted,
mn77:33.11: and an unexalted mind as unexalted;
mn77:33.12: they understand a surpassable mind as surpassable,
mn77:33.13: and an unsurpassable mind as unsurpassable;
mn77:33.14: they understand a concentrated mind as concentrated,
mn77:33.15: and an unconcentrated mind as unconcentrated;
mn77:33.16: they understand a liberated mind as liberated,
mn77:33.17: and an unliberated mind as unliberated.
mn77:33.18: Just as, Udāyī, a woman or a man, young, youthful, and fond of ornaments, looking at the reflection of her own face in a clean, bright mirror or in a bowl of clear water, would know if there were a blemish: ‘there is a blemish’, or would know if there were no blemish: ‘there is no blemish’;
mn77:33.19: so too, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples, having encompassed the minds of other beings and other persons with their own minds, understand them—
mn77:33.20: they understand a mind with lust as a mind with lust,
mn77:33.35: and an unliberated mind as unliberated.
mn77:33.36: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.
mn77:34.1: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples recollect their manifold past lives, that is, one birth, two births, three births, four births, five births, ten births, twenty births, thirty births, forty births, fifty births, a hundred births, a thousand births, a hundred thousand births, many aeons of world-contraction, many aeons of world-expansion, many aeons of world-contraction and expansion:[^10] ‘there I was so named, of such a clan, with such an appearance, such was my food, such my experience of pleasure and pain, such my life-span; and passing away from there, I reappeared elsewhere; and there too I was so named, of such a clan, with such an appearance, such was my food, such my experience of pleasure and pain, such my life-span; and passing away from there, I reappeared here’—thus they recollect their manifold past lives with their aspects and particulars.
mn77:34.2: Just as, Udāyī, a man might go from his own village to another village, and from that village go on to yet another village, and from that village come back again to his own village; he would think thus: ‘I went from my own village to that village, and there I stood thus, sat thus, spoke thus, was silent thus; and from that village I went on to that other village, and there too I stood thus, sat thus, spoke thus, was silent thus; and from that village I have come back again to my own village’;
mn77:34.3: so too, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples recollect their manifold past lives, that is, one birth … thus they recollect their manifold past lives with their aspects and particulars.
mn77:34.4: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.
mn77:35.1: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples, with the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, see beings passing away and reappearing, inferior and superior, fair and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate, and understand how beings pass on according to their actions: ‘these beings who were ill-conducted in body, speech, and mind, revilers of the noble ones, wrong in view, undertaking action based on wrong view, on the dissolution of the body, after death, have reappeared in a state of deprivation, in a bad destination, in perdition, even in hell; but these beings who were well-conducted in body, speech, and mind, not revilers of the noble ones, right in view, undertaking action based on right view, on the dissolution of the body, after death, have reappeared in a good destination, even in the heavenly world’—thus, with the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, they see beings passing away and reappearing, inferior and superior, fair and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate, and understand how beings pass on according to their actions.
mn77:35.2: Just as, Udāyī, there might be two houses with doors, and a man with good eyes standing between them might see people entering a house and leaving it, walking to and fro;
mn77:35.3: so too, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples, with the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, see beings passing away and reappearing … and understand how beings pass on according to their actions …
mn77:35.4: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.
mn77:36.1: Again, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples, by realizing for themselves with direct knowledge, here and now enter upon and abide in the deliverance of mind and the deliverance by wisdom that are taintless with the exhaustion of the taints.
mn77:36.2: Just as, Udāyī, there might be a lake of water in a mountain recess, clear, limpid, and undisturbed, and a man with good eyes, standing on the bank, might see shells, gravel, and pebbles, and also shoals of fish swimming about and resting; he would think thus: ‘This lake of water is clear, limpid, and undisturbed, and there are these shells, gravel, and pebbles, and also these shoals of fish swimming about and resting’;
mn77:36.3: so too, Udāyī, I have proclaimed to my disciples the way, practising which my disciples, by realizing for themselves with direct knowledge, here and now enter upon and abide in the deliverance of mind and the deliverance by wisdom that are taintless with the exhaustion of the taints.
mn77:36.4: And, practising this, many of my disciples dwell having reached the consummation and perfection of direct knowledge.
mn77:37.1: This, Udāyī, is the fifth thing on account of which my disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me.
mn77:38.1: These, Udāyī, are the five things on account of which my disciples honour, respect, revere, and venerate me, and live in dependence on me, honouring and respecting me.”
mn77:38.2: This is what the Blessed One said.
mn77:38.3: Sakuludāyī the Wanderer was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.
